title: Chicken drumstick, baked, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the lower part of the thigh, containing meat, skin and a small bone. When baked in the oven with a coating, the skin becomes crispy while the meat stays juicy. This preparation is popular in many world cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Drumsticks are often used in dishes where juiciness and flavor are key, such as barbecues or casseroles.
Baking with a coating creates a crunchy crust without the need for large amounts of oil.
Chicken skin is rich in collagen, which turns into gelatin during cooking and supports joint health.
In some countries drumsticks are served with barbecue sauce, in others with spicy rubs.
Drumsticks are a more affordable source of protein compared with breast fillets.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: They contain B3 (niacin) and B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Iron, zinc and phosphorus in the meat support blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Skin supplies collagen
items.content: Eating the skin adds extra collagen, beneficial for skin and joints.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Drumsticks have virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Drumsticks contain more fat than breast meat, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Improper cooking can leave meat undercooked, increasing the risk of foodborne illness.

items.title: Salt in coating
items.content: Pre‑made coatings often contain high sodium; choose low‑salt versions if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken drumsticks can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, added to soups, or used in sandwiches. The skin and coating are eaten together, providing crunch and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh drumsticks in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen drumsticks last up to 9 months in the freezer. Before cooking, check for off‑odors or discoloration; discard if any are present.
